name: Nauuo and Circle
description: Nauuo is a girl who loves drawing circles. One day she has drawn a circle and wanted to draw a tree on it. The tree is a connected undirected graph consisting of $$$n$$$ nodes and $$$n-1$$$ edges. The nodes are numbered from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$. Nauuo wants to draw a tree on the circle, the nodes of the tree should be in $$$n$$$ distinct points on the circle, and the edges should be straight without crossing each other. "Without crossing each other" means that every two edges have no common point or the only common point is an endpoint of both edges. Nauuo wants to draw the tree using a permutation of $$$n$$$ elements. A permutation of $$$n$$$ elements is a sequence of integers $$$p_1,p_2,\ldots,p_n$$$ in which every integer from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$ appears exactly once. After a permutation is chosen Nauuo draws the $$$i$$$-th node in the $$$p_i$$$-th point on the circle, then draws the edges connecting the nodes. The tree is given, Nauuo wants to know how many permutations are there so that the tree drawn satisfies the rule (the edges are straight without crossing each other). She only wants to know the answer modulo $$$998244353$$$, can you help her? It is obvious that whether a permutation is valid or not does not depend on which $$$n$$$ points on the circle are chosen.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2\le n\le 2\cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of nodes in the tree. Each of the next $$$n-1$$$ lines contains two integers $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$ ($$$1\le u,v\le n$$$), denoting there is an edge between $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$. It is guaranteed that the given edges form a tree.
output_specification: The output contains a single integer — the number of permutations suitable to draw the given tree on a circle satisfying the rule, modulo $$$998244353$$$.
approach_summary: Define tree DP state dp[u][state] computing optimal subproblem values for the subtree rooted at u. Aggregate transitions across children in post-order traversal in O(N × S) time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1172B — Nauuo and Circle [463. DP on Trees and DAGs]
topic_editorial.summary: Tree Dynamic Programming with post-order traversal.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: A rooted tree has a clean hierarchical structure: removing the root decomposes the tree into independent disjoint subtrees. Therefore, the optimal solution for a subtree rooted at vertex $u$ depends purely on the solutions of its direct children $v \in \text{children}(u)$.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Root Selection & State Definition
Arbitrarily root the tree at node $1$. Define:
- $dp[u][0] = $ optimal value for the subtree of $u$ if node $u$ is excluded.
- $dp[u][1] = $ optimal value for the subtree of $u$ if node $u$ is included.

### Step 2: Post-Order DFS Traversal
We traverse the tree using depth-first search. A node $u$ computes its answers only after all its children $v \in \text{adj}[u]$ have computed theirs:
$$\text{dfs}(u, \text{parent})$$

### Step 3: Subtree Transition
For each child $v$ of $u$ ($v \ne \text{parent}$):
$$dp[u][0] = \sum_{v} \max(dp[v][0], dp[v][1])$$
$$dp[u][1] = \text{val}[u] + \sum_{v} dp[v][0]$$

### Step 4: Final Answer
At the root:
$$\text{Ans} = \max(dp[1][0], dp[1][1])$$
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  Each node and edge in the tree is visited exactly once during the DFS traversal. All transitions at node $u$ run in time proportional to its degree. Summing across all vertices: $\sum \text{deg}(u) = 2(N-1) = \mathcal{O}(N)$.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  Adjacency list storage takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory, DP state arrays take $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory, and the DFS call stack takes at most $\mathcal{O}(N)$ depth in the worst case.
